content: 1. Valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to valsartan. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Omeprazole may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during secretin stimulation testing, potentially leading to a false diagnosis of gastrinoma. Discontinue omeprazole at least 14 days before testing to allow gastrin levels to normalize. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. 6. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose and resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 8. Clarithromycin and sertraline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Clarithromycin and sevoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with clarithromycin is not recommended due to increased systemic exposure to sildenafil. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting both P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, significantly increasing the risk of rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting both P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora necessary for drug activation. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, reducing velpatasvir solubility. Co-administration with omeprazole or other PPIs is not recommended. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Clarithromycin and sorafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Clarithromycin and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. If co-administration with acid-reducing agents is unavoidable, administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after the acid-reducing agent. 22. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Omeprazole decreases the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin and omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism, respectively. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for altered effects. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of streptomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OATP1-mediated active secretion. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Clarithromycin and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. 32. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases tacrolimus levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole and clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 39. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 40. Clarithromycin and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 41. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of temocillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels of theophylline by decreasing its metabolism. Omeprazole increases theophylline toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Thioridazine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Omeprazole decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by increasing gastric pH. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 51. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
